item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Weekly Parsha Points - VaYishlach (“He sent”) — Are You Authentic? on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

VaYishlach (“He sent”)

Are You Authentic ?

Part 1

Last week, in parsha VaYetzei, we read about Jacob leaving his comfortable home and familiar surroundings in Beersheba to go forth to Padan-aram in Mesopotamia, and visit his parents’ relatives. In doing so, Jacob was taking his first steps toward fulfilling his destiny and becoming spiritually transformed in the process.

Real followers pass the test.

Central truth: The Father loves us too much to allow us to remain in the same spiritual place and condition for long, or settle back in familiar but unprofitable comfort zones. He wants us to continue to grow stronger in faith and move unto deeper and more intimate fellowship with Him. Our Messiah spoke to His disciples in this way: “If you abide [ obey, endure, stay in place] in my word, you are truly my disciples.” Understand: What this phrase, “truly my disciples” implies is that there are disciples who are not truly disciples. The word “truly” means “really”--as in ”really my disciples.” In any case, it has been said that a life without duty, discipline, or commitment, i.e. purpose, is bereft of satisfaction and joy. Do you agree?

Created for good works.

In other words there are real and unreal disciples who do not conform to or care about the teaching of Yeshua. There are both authentic and inauthentic disciples in the Church. The imposters are not led by the Holy Spirit. Consider: There is discipleship that is merely outward (a big show), and a discipleship that is faith-filled, inspirational, and completely sincere. So, to which group do you really belong, dear reader. “If you abide [obey] in My Word” is the test. Genuine disciples have eternity in their vision and are positioned for victory and blessing as they grow into overcomers and mature as the Bride of Messiah. See Revelation 2 and 3.

Steps to Discipleship.

This week, in parsha VaYishlach, we read the record of Jacob’s flight from Padan-aram back to Beersheba. However, it appears that his eventful return did not go quite as he had envisioned. The report of his troubled trek back to Canaan could be given this way: “A man’s heart devises the way; but the LORD directs his steps” (Proverbs 16:9). This is very good news for all attentive believers, wouldn’t you say?

The reminder applies to the Christian believers of this age, and also to the descendants of the scattered tribes of the House of Israel who are endeavoring to return to and settle into their Hebraic, Torah-based heritage. This is the birthright blessing attained by believers through their faith in Messiah Yeshua as Savior and sole Mediator of the New Covenant. Hebrews 8:6;12:24. But be informed. Modern saints have been called to contend for [recover and restore] the Torah and Spirit rooted faith that was once delivered to the apostolic, New Covenant Judean Ecclesia (Kahal). Over the centuries however, this faith been compromised, vitiated, and broken apart by false teachings and wandering religious orthodoxies. Determination and endurance are the pre-requisites for recovering the original New Testament apostolic faith and abiding in its truth. This presents a duty to modern disciples.

Parsha VaYishlach (“He sent’)

References: Genesis 32:3-36:43; Hosea 11:7-12:12; Joshua 11:5-19; First Corinthians 5:1-13; Revelation 7:1-12.

Apply the features of Jacob’s journey to your own.

We cannot cover in detail the complete narrative of this rich parsha in our “Points” briefing. However, we will glean relevant lessons from the narrative of Jacob’s journey home to Beersheba. Dear reader, you will be inspired by witnessing his climatic spiritual transformation which occurred during his eventful trek homeward. Goal: Start abiding in the light of divine truth known to you just as the patriarch did when he set out on his arduous journey. You will learn that no matter what resistance or trials you encounter, as you honor Yahweh you will be become transformed as well, but into your Savior’s likeness. Such is a wonderful opportunity, and privilege! Hence it is written: “Trust in YHWH with all thine heart and lean not on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge Him and He shall direct your paths” (Proverbs 3:5-6). So, let’s consider the following six points.

Providential Oversight.

  1. 1. “...return to the land of your fathers..“ (Gen, 31:3). After twenty years of serving his father-in-law Laban in Padam-aram, Yahweh directed Jacob to return to Canaan, the land of his father Abraham. And Jacob went, taking his family and flocks with him, and Yahweh’s reassuring promises, such as: ”I will be with you.” Such an affirmation would be hugely encouraging to any traveler. We have ours too, as we walk the narrow spoken of by Yeshua! Remember Matthew 28:16-20 and Joshua 1:9. Notwithstanding, Jacob left Padan-aram but shortly afterwards was confronted by Laban who pursued him. Their issues were settled with a covenant. Learn: Trust in your Father’s faithfulness and compassionate care, friend, concerning any confrontation or circumstance that suddenly comes upon you.

A heavenly escort. How good is that?

2. “...the angels of God met him“ (32:1). Jacob continued southward to the Jabbok River where heavenly angels, the messengers of Almighty God, intercepted him [fell in with him]. He was informed by his new escort service that Esau was nearby, and to be prepared. Note: This encounter was not just a vision, it was a supernatural manifestation of heavenly ministers. Jacob recognized them as God’s host–or Mananeh. Learn: A heavenly escort is an emblem of angelic guardianship which “encampeth round about them that fear [reverence and trust] the LORD and delivereth them…” and “..keepeth them in all their ways” (Psalms 34 and 91). That includes you, dear reader. You are highly valued and your faith journey is being chaperoned by a heaavenly escort, even now!

Be courageous and strong. Be not dismayed or afraid.

3. “Then the messengers returned...“ (32:6). Having learned of Esau’s approach, Jacob “...sent messengers before him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom’” (B’resheit 32:3). They returned to inform the weary traveler that his brother had 400 armed men with him. Jacob feared violent consequences could occur during this “reunion” so he acted quickly and wisely. The dutiful patriarch divided his family and flocks into two camps behind him. And he prayed, “Oh God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, Oh LORD…deliver me I pray thee”. Jacob prayed with humility and intensity unto YHWH who—as pointed out already, had made wonderful promises to his fathers of which he was the heir. Learn: He says to you personally: “The LORD your God is with you. He is mighty to save. He will take great delight in you, He will quiet you with His love, He will rejoice over you with singing” (Zephaniah 3:17). Reader, hold to your hope.

Give gifts. It Works.

4. “...so he took what came to his hand…” (32:13). Jacob believed the threat he perceived could not actually be reconciled. It appeared to him that the looming rapproachment [the restoration of happy relations] was beyond his ability to handle. So he sought the one who said, “I will surely do good and make your seed as the sand of the sea.” Jacob was given wisdom, the most valuable tool for handling confrontations—i. e., spiritual warfare. Hence, sent a series of gifts–herds and flocks–to soften the temperament of Esau and show respect to his older brother with courteous words, such as referring to him as “my master.” As a result, their meeting was amiable, and after friendly exchanges and assurances they separated. Then Jacob sent his family over the Jabbok tributary but he remained alone. Learn: Kindness and courtesy honor Yahweh and work wonders with your fellow man.

Soft words break bones–stubbornness.

5. “In this manner you shall speak to him…” (32:19). Jacob grew in wisdom and his experience had given him an acute understanding of human nature. He learned that kindness and warm words could soften a hard heart. “I will appease him with a present.” Learn: A repetition of generous presents would act upon Esau in the same way a blacksmith’s hammer, through repeated strikes, shapes the posture of hot iron. There would be a notable effect on the brothers’ reunion by way of Jacob’s wise action–-the fruit of an affectionate reunion. Learn: The Holy One of Israel acknowledges and blesses a generous giver. Remember the poor widow and her two-penny offering? She’s in the Bible’s Hall of Fame for eternity, friend, and rich beyond calculation.

Engage in unrelenting prayer.

6. “Then Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him…” ( 32:22-32). In the verse we witness the mysterious wrestling match between Jacob and a man we interpret to be the visible, physical representation of the invisible Elohim. The confrontation occurred abruptly at a time when Jacob was engrossed in devout, heartfelt prayer. The contest was indeed a physical effort, but foremost it was an intense struggle preoccupying the soul of Jacob. He wanted and needed an enduring blessing, as do many of us today. However, he was given first a dislocated hip, of all thing! Yet Jacob persisted in striving with his heavenly Opponent. Point: Perhaps the dislocated hip was a sign and reminder that Jacob would never succeed in fulfilling his destiny by depending upon his own human strength and carnal temperament. Rather, such would be accomplished only by full reliance on the Almighty. Period. The Contender, allowed Jacob to prevail, and graciously gave him a blessed new name, Israel. It means “one who prevails with God and man.” Learn: Emulate Jacob. Here’s your verse. Live it! “Let us not grow weary in doing good, for in due season we will reap if we don’t give up” (Gal. 6:9). Keep Persevering, blessed reader.

Conclusion of VaYishlach, Part 1

The featured confrontation took place on the north side of the Jabbok river at night where Jacob had been alone, communing in his heart and making supplication and confession. It was at that time of focused prayer the heavenly Visitor suddenly approached him and the physical struggle began. Learn: 1. Set aside an altar time of reading and prayer every day. 2. Increase your attention span. 3. Start listening for His voice. 5. Abide in His Word. Point: Your Elohim, who hears, is bigger than your troubles and stronger than your enemies. He will bless you, reader, according to your need. Therefore, keep seeking his face. Trust His promises. Deepen your relationship with Him, Shaddai–Almighty God—the All Sufficient One. And especially be baptized in the Holy Spirit and Fire. and you will do well. Amen.

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Part 2 is next: It points out the lessons coming out

from Shechem from which we can benefit. Let’s go there together and walk together with Jacob. Hutch Church Shalom.

item.description: Personal Transformation. Will you pay the Price?
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Parsha Points - Parsha VaYeitzei (“He went out”) on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Parsha VaYeitzei (“He went out”)

Personal Transformation. Will you pay the Price?

Part 2

A life-changing encounter for Jacob.

At night, on his return journey home, Jacob came to the River Jabbok. He sent his large

family across the river and was afterwards left alone. Then, as it is written: “... a man

wrestled with him until the breaking of the day.” How the contest started we are not informed. Nevertheless, when the man saw that he did not prevail against Jacob, he put his hip out of socket as they wrestled. Then he said, “Let me go because the day has broken.” But Jacob said, “I will not let you go until you bless me.” And he said, “What is your name?” And the young sojourner said, “Jacob.” Then he said, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with God and man and have prevailed.” Genesis 34:24-28. Note: There are several standards to point out that contributed to Jacob’s transformation into a new man, “Israel.” And these points could inspire you as well, reader, depending on your spiritual ambition of course.

1.The reluctance to release his opponent, even when his thigh joint had been dislocated, indicates Jacob’s unwavering determination to be blessed by God in a meaningful and most needed way. Point: Despite circumstances, a modern saint must also persevere in fervent prayer before the Throne of Grace. The believer is instructed to pray always with “all prayer and supplication in the Spirit” (Ephesians 6:18).

2. Jacob was given a new name, Israel. It makes a statement that Jacob was one who would strive with the Almighty until he prevailed. Point: Friend, do likewise! Set your course to excel as an overcomer. Strive with Yahweh to be blessed in this worthy campaign and you will also receive a new name from Yeshua, your High Priest. Revelation 2:17!

3. Jacob was spiritually elevated by the blessing bestowed upon him and came to understand the importance of God’s favor and his need for providential care. Point: Seek to honor Him in all things. Learn to be led and instructed by the Holy Spirit.. Wisdom is a weapon of warfare. Ephesians 1:18!

4. The circumstances of his previous years had changed Jacob, yet the Jabbok River event positioned Jacob in a higher spiritual level altogether. Jacob embraced the true God and His precepts as did His father Isaac, and grandfather, Abraham. [Their instruction likely came from Shem who was alive at that time.] Point: Jacob learned obedience. New Covenant saint, grow up and learn obedience too. There’s no room for hypocrisy in your quest to rank among the blessed overcomers. You may also have divine, life-changing divine encounters with Elohim, your Creator. Expect to hear His voice by the Spirit and encounter His presence in a discernable way. Get baptized in the Holy Spirit. See: Acts 1:1-9 and 2.1-47; 10:44-46; 19:6; 1 Cor. 14.

Follow Yahweh’s truth, not the endless banter humans.

Obedience is not legalism. It is the pure, biblical demonstration of faith and love for our Creator and Redeemer. You and I can spend months – pursuing and engaging political conflicts, advancing technology, assorted ideologies, financial upheavals and their threats, war, and religious inventions and controversies, to cite a few common preoccupations. But all that stuff will, in time, become repetitive and wearisome. Point: As Solomon realized as he drew close to his death, man’s chief duty is to obey God’s sacred Word. Our battle’s core is spiritual–always. If we won’t follow our Master after “His manner,” we will continue to abide under a demonic curse. Selah. 2 Chronicles 7:14 waits to be fiulfilled. “If my people, who are called…” You know the rest. But did you know that without obedience to known, applicable, and doable Scriptural truth there is no real repentance and no true discipleship? Pray. Wait upon the Spirit of Truth to come alongside you. And remember the plight of King Saul.

Peniel:

Did you know that locations can leave an impression on people that causes changes in their world view, stirs introspection, and even inspires personal development. Thus the Almighty chooses appropriate places for His work with people. Jacob named the place of his encounter with the heavenly wrestler, Peniel. The generally accepted meaning of the name is: For I have seen God face to face. However, since no human can see Elohim’s face and live, the name could refer to a close, spiritually intimate interaction. Keep in mind, friend. You can do your own research and decide for yourself concerning anything written in our blogs. This has always been our counsel concerning what Contenders Voice ministries happen to teach.

Note: Following this amazing visitation, an existential work of grace, Jacob went forward fully prepared to meet and be reconciled with his once-hostile brother, Esau.

The Torah is the standard of Discipleship

The study of the Torah is essential for Christians, and everyone else, for that matter. The Torah’s origin is divine, it is not restricted, but has a universal application. “It has been evident that believers, including preachers, often interpret the Bible through the lens of their culture, worldview, and public education. This has resulted in many misleading religious beliefs, doctrines and practices becoming prevalent in the Christianity that are not in accord with the clear and pure teachings of the holy Scriptures. Lamentably, this is often the case with the evangelical church in the United States. This country is strongly influential across the globe. Hence, the American evangelical system has also produced a strong influence worldwide. This has occurred by the exportation of a westernized gospel replete with an American pattern of faith that is not in line with the Hebraic paradigm of Scripture. Consequently, in the United States pulpit preaching usually comes across looking more like “American Dream” and “Self-actualization” lessons than the Torah-based and Spirit-powered Gospel. Unabridged, expository proclamations are what is needed now. VaYetzei’s related three closing points should find applications in your own lives, my persistent friends.

He will visit you.

Point 1. “Jacob departed…and encountered a place and spent the night there…” (10-11). The location of Jacob’s encounter with Yeshua was Mount Moriah, the site where Abraham bound Isaac on the altar and where the Temple would later stand. Point: For disciples to desire a visitation of the Holy One of Israel is biblical. Learn: Jacob is a type of each one of us who is awakening and coming to our biblical heritage. The ladder in his dream is seen as Yeshua’s cross of atonement which was situated on earth and still reaches into heaven, for it was the divine mediator who was sacrificed upon it. He now stands above the cross and speaks to the heirs of salvation–His chosen: “I will never leave you.” Point: In our own journeys to our prescribed destinies may our daily times of prayer, praise, study, and service result in divine encounters with Elohim at the gate of glory. Moses pleaded :“Please show me your glory.” Yahweh responds: “I will do this very thing you have asked…” (Exodus 33:18). Moses had found favor in God’s sight. WHY? What’s your answer?

You are sent also. What is your purpose?

Point 2. “And he went out…” Jacob’s life teaches attentive believers that each of us has

a familiar past, an old life, a family and even a religion of some sort from which we must separate in order to go forward and accept the challenge of pursuing Yahweh’s prophetic truth and make our own contribution to the restoration of all things spoken of by the prophets–including both the houses of Israel. Learn: When Jacob went out to face his tests of faith and pursue his destiny, Elohim’s voice spoke to him, personally assuring Jacob that the Most High Elohim would be in continual attendance with him in his pilgrimage just as He was with his fathers. Point: As Jacob was sent by Isaac, each saint today has been sent forth by their Good Shepherd, Yeshua. “Go ye therefore…and I am with you…” (Matthew 28:18-20).

Transformative, purifying Holy Fire

Point 3. Reader, you have a heavenly Helper! Yield to His leading. It is written: “But when he, the Spirit of Truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he will not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will show you things to come” (John 16:3). Learn: For New Testament saints to be changed from a Jacob into an Israel we need an internal spiritual fire. Hence, every saint would do well to be baptized by Yeshua with the Holy Spirit, as I mentioned earlier. This experience is a gift that (1) gives power and (2) enhances faith and zeal for the recipients to live for Yeshua and follow His instructions.

Get Zeal !

Our High Priest, Yeshua, is the Kingdom’s Lawgiver. Some of His modern saints are beginning to love the Father’s precepts, judgments, testimonies, statutes, and commandments exceedingly. It is fitting. Point: Because of their faith in and love for their Shepherd, His followers (sheep) want to live zealously by His laws and standards, i.e., boldly follow His instructions. See Romans 16:25-26; Hebrews 10:16).

Cross over to New Wine

One of Jacob’s “life lessons” shows us that although each believer in Messiah Yeshua has a familiar past, an old life, a family, or even a religion, we must separate from old, unholy influences. This is called sanctification--being set apart for Yahweh purposes. It is necessary for advancing forward and meeting the challenge of pursuing Yahweh’s prophetic word. Our call is to make a contribution to the restoration of all things spoken of by the prophets (Acts 3:21). When Jacob left his family and went out to face his tests of faith and pursue his destiny, Elohim spoke to him, personally. Jacob was assured that the Most High would be in continual attendance with him in his pilgrimage, just as He was with his fathers. Point: As Jacob was sent by Isaac, each New Covenant, Spirit-born believer in Yeshua is sent also, and accompanied by His Spirit. It is written: “He will not let your foot slip–he who watches over you will not slumber” (Psalm 121:3-4). Therefore, reader, cast your anxieties on Him. He cares for you. So go forward on your faith pathway to spiritual maturity. Review Matthew 28:18-20; Hebrews 6:1-3.

Our job: Teach His people to obey His precepts and judgments.

It is the Messiah’s will that the truth, standards, and principles of His Law [His teaching; instructions for life and worship] would be fulfilled in the lives of His followers (Romans 3:31; 8:4). Understand: Our High Priest, Yeshua, is the Kingdom’s Lawgiver. His modern saints are awakening spiritually and beginning to love the Father’s precepts, judgments, testimonies, statutes, and commandments exceedingly. It is fitting. Point: Because of their faith in and love for their Shepherd, His followers (sheep) want to live by His laws and standards, i.e., to follow His instructions. See Romans 16:25-26 and Hebrews 10:16. This is His way!

We will continue to study Jacob’s life in greater detail in the next five parshas of Genesis by highlighting its most relevant features. It is profitable to first understand how the patriarch’s life, social status, and prophetic family vision relate to that of believers today–which includes you and myself, your Parsha Points host. Next week’s Parsha is VaYishlach (“And he sent”). Its narrative covers Jacob and his family’s flight from Beersheba to Padan-aram. We will glean helpful, personally advantageous lessons from this parsha.

Until next week, here’s a prophetic Scripture and a poem for you to read and contemplate.

“Ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein.”

Jeremiah 6:16

What does that mean to you?

Learn Faith and Works are Bonded

item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Constructing the Golden Age on a Solid Rock on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Part 1

So, what's next? Well, the Golden Age for America is on the table now. Are its dreamers envisioning an expansive empire or an age of great social prosperity founded upon life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness? Time will tell the tale.

Blessed reader, the new executive orders now coming to bear upon America--those which were immediately signed following the recent inauguration and the promise of other governmental upgrades to come--are foundational accomplishments setting a tenor of hopeful expectation for our nation's restoration. Will the coming executive corrections (a) turn back our wobbly culture's spreading problems of lawlessness, social confliction, and governmental disorders--and (b) galvanize the building of the nation into a spiritual, moral, scientific, and financial bastion in the world? I would say the political, break-through steps of our new administration are proving effectual, and therefore it could easily be likened unto a political icebreaker--reminiscent of the heavy vessels of old which were reinforced with a strong and heavy bows that plowed into resistant artic ice flows and broke them up, thus allowing open passage to otherwise stifled maritime activity. In a similar manner, Trump is opening political passageways for social change. Though obstacles to restoration progress are being removed, some ask—is working to establish a golden age--a period of greatly amplified prosperity for our nation, a reasonable undertaking? Is it heaven sent, or the object of someone’s imagination? We do notice that the current changes are building excitement and stirring new vision for a profound resuscitation of the fading American Dream. Yet, there are two primary streams of vision emerging and both are needed to fulfill the hope of secular and spiritual restoration for the country. One is secular and involves the restoration of societal security, and profound, existential technological innovation. The other is spiritual and involves the restoration of full biblical truth and its incorporation into a conflicted institutional Ecclesia as the spiritual platform that can sustain a moral, liberty-friendly renewal. Both, working in their defined spheres can together bring beneficial changes to the country. But, on the other hand, can two unmixable visions of humane prosperity, if not properly related, produce favorable results. It's unlikely. After all, Scripture does contain this instruction --> "Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together" (Deut. 22:10). Why not, you ask? It is because they are physically unbalanced and could not plow a straight furrow together. Most significantly however, a careful look at Scripture reveals that any enterprise, large or small, must be constructed according to the instructions of the Messiah in order to resist institutionalism and endure the storms of life. See Matthew 7:24-27. Therefore, may we evaluate the matter of a national golden age and then decide for ourselves how our cultural recovery should be undertaken. But first, we should refresh our musing with another look at the Holy Spirit's sacred counsel posted above: "...let all you do be done in love" (1 Corinthians16:13). This would have to be the long term project's Prime Directive. It represents wisdom and thus welcomes the outstretched hand of Yahweh to assist and coordinate our labors to restore our nation on a foundation of stable biblical truth. Therefore, let's consider thoughtfully the transformation of America that is getting underway; what is transpiring in the land regarding the Golden Age vision, and where each one of us can fit in and become an active part of this great and exciting drama.

Bear in mind brethren, our new president in not in office by happenstance. He has been fore-ordained to occupy his high leadership position and is providentially set in place-while in good health, by divine intervention. He is thus the premier end-time player, so to speak. There are advantaged reasons why Yahweh wants to use our president and his administration. These favorable purposes include, for instance: (1) restoring our constitutional republic's culture and government, (2) elevating and preparing America for leadership during the turbulent times ahead, (3) supporting Israel for a season of peace, political unification, and Temple-building, (4) stabilizing other nations, and (5) moving Yahweh's prophetic, restoration timeclock forward--while this president remains in office. Therefore, we who support a spiritual and morally renewed and secured country with capable righteous leadership in place must pray daily for our president and his administrative team in order that Yahweh's purposes can indeed be fulfilled while he is in office. The LORD will do great things for us if we humble ourselves, repent, and follow His instructions of life. Consider what is written: "The reward for humility and fear of the LORD [devotion; piety] is riches, honor, and life" (Proverbs 22:4 NAS; Brackets C.V.). Amen!

Part 2

While building a golden age for the nation, the whole world is heading to a catastrophic end. Revelation 18-22. The Old Testament book of Daniel, chapter 7, speaks of the rise and fall of empires and directs our attention to the advent of the eternal Kingdom of the Most High which His holy people will inherit and indwell throughout eternity. How wonderful a prospect to be held before us! Meanwhile, the world is undergoing radical changes which are setting it up for the fulfillment of prophecy. Consider the seven seals of Revelation 6, for instance. The seals are historical and futuristic also. The first four seals describe the foremost spiritual forces that have accompanied and shaped history from the first century CE all the way to this point in time--which is most likely Seal 5. It references the blood of the martyrs. Note: We modern, western believes need to grasp what Christian life can be like in foreign nations. Thousands of Christians are killed for their faith each year, and more than 365 million Christians face extreme hostilities, persecution, imprisonment each year also. Further, abduction, sexual abuse, broken families, and destroyed homes are experienced regularly in hostile regimes. Please pray for those who live in restricted countries. Seal 6 follows and it appears to be a time of limited nuclear warfare and widespread societal turmoil — aka, NWO earthquakes. These events make necessary a multi-year period of widespread recovery and rebuilding to take place in preparation for the Antichrist. Enter Seal 7, noted for the 1/2 hour of silence occurring in heaven. According to the Kepha principle (2 Peter 3:8) -- this 30 minute quietude, we are told, translates into 20.67 years, which is an adequate time frame needed on earth for a new generation to be inculcated with Scientism's transhumanist propaganda, rebuilding war torn regions, cleaning up and burying the war debris, raising a temple in Israel, a NWO to arise and re-establish a global Artificial Intelligence grid, and create a entirely digitalized prison planet. That’s a lot. When the first Trumpet sounds the tribulation period as recorded in Revelation chapter 8 officially begins. The bowls of judgment come upon the planet after the seventh trumpet has been sounded as recorded in Revelation, chapter 11.

As we go to Part 2, keep in mind friends, that Contender's Voice is not founded to inform seekers and readers only, but to encourage all who visit us to develop friendship-faith in the risen Messiah, the fear of the Almighty, and a willing compliance to His Scriptures. These basic commitments will enhance your spiritual prosperity, peace, and bring joy into one’s life and service. Therefore, may all His saints seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and align their ambitions and life goals with His Holy Word and prophetic purposes. And secondly--may we hold up our constitutional republic as loyal patriots, and participate in its restoration and elevation. Conclusion: The Golden Age of America should be constructed upon the foundation of unabridged Scripture. Therefore, brethren, follow daily the sacred words of Messiah Yeshua which direct His followers to "seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness" (Mt. 6:33).

Conclusion

We live in an age marked by powerful, unrelenting evil forces--the hellish components producing spiritual and secular deception throughout the land. They are undergirded by the active and sentient spiritual wickedness of the second heaven that houses the highly organized, multitudinous dark empire of Satan. Do not dismiss this reality. Apostle John himself declared that the "...whole world lies in the power of the evil one" (1 John 5:19-20). Its rank and file are comprised of legions of fallen angels and multitudinous demons that relentlessly work to corrupt the minds of ignorant, unprotected people, and energize them for several nefarious purposes. They include (1) relentlessly opposing Yahweh's Gospel while luring believers into sinful lifestyles, (2) obfuscating Torah-based truth with false teaching, (3) causing the Ecclesia to avoid the Holy Spirit's full ministry, (4) disparaging biblical moral standards throughout the nations, (5) mocking holiness and righteousness, (6) disparaging the blessed truth about Yeshua--the divine Son, and His atonement, (7) causing mental and even physical disorders, and more. Ephesians 6:12. These beings comprise the unseen (usually) enemies of mankind. Yeshua's dedicated followers are distinguished by their (a) separation from following worldly ideologies, circular philosophies, New Age beliefs, and faulty moral standards and their (b) compliance instead to His instructions and teachings alone. Indeed, may all His followers be spiritually elevated by becoming genuine disciples who hear His commands with wise and submitted hearts. Yet the question arises: Which of Elohim's commandments do we obey for there are many. That's true. The Torah contains hundreds of moral, ceremonial, civil and national laws. Someone may therefore think that obeying the greatest laws is more important that striving to honor the least of the laws. But is that so? The greatest law, according the our Torah teacher, Yeshua, is found in Deuteronomy 6: 5, where it is written: "You shall love the LORD you God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength." This command is foremost and well known. It is accomplished by love-motivated believers obeying His instructions--all that are known to them, understood, applicable, and doable. That would be the starting point, so to speak. But what about the lesser known laws in the Torah? Are they important as well? Yes, they are! All God's laws reflect His sublime, holy character and agape love for His creation and all those abiding within it. So let's examine a couple of the lesser known laws and discover that their purpose is connected to honoring YHWH and even loving our neighbor, as are the better known ones. Leviticus 19:18. John 14:15-21.

"If you happen to come upon a bird's nest along the way...you shall not take the mother with the young, but the young you may take...in order that it may be well with you and that you may prolong your days" (22: 6-7).

The Jewish commentator Rambam cited two reasons for this unusual prohibition: (1) It is cruel to kill a mother and its young together, on the same day (Lev. 22:28). (2) The statute implied that Israelites must be restrained from endangering any species of animals, which could happen if there were no restrictions on slaughtering a mother animal with its young. Contender's Voice adds: (3) The female sex makes motherhood and the propagation of young possible, and binds one generation to the next. Thus, the command to spare the mother bird is significant, for the principle conveys the same consideration to other species of animals, and also accentuates the verse (v. 5) it follows concerning differentiating between the sexes. (4) The mother was spared for a purely practical reason: because the female is needed for continuing the propagation [increase in numbers] of birds, and maintaining their population. Birds were needed! They kept down bugs, insects, and grubs, and even helped pollinate the fields. (5) The statute, which rendered motherhood sacred in the woods, helped remind Israel how much more should motherhood be sacred in the nation. A mother should be honored by her children. To the perceptive, the seemingly insignificant law taught that the young should bear the burdens, not the old. (6) Then, there is the law prohibiting boiling (seething) a kid in its mother's milk, that is thrice repeated in Scripture, and relates to the "nest" statute. See: Exodus 23:19; 34:26, and Deut. 14:21.

The three-fold repetition of the law indicates its importance in helping to keep awake the sense of propriety and respect for life in the soul of the nation. There are various explanations for this statute, but upon this there is agreement: It is "...a protest against cruelty, and outraging [of] the order of nature, more especially the peculiarly sacred portion of nature's order, the tender relation between parent and child, mother and suckling. No doubt the practice existed. [Goat] kids were thought more palatable [tasty] when boiled in milk; and the mother's milk was the readiest to obtain. But in this way the mother was made sort of [an] accomplice in the death of her [young], which men were induced to kill on account of the flavor that her milk gave it...but feeling revolts from it, and [so does] the general sense of civilized mankind..." Eerdmans, Book of the Covenant, p. 203. (7) The statute carried with it an incentive, a great promise, similar to that of the fifth commandment: "Thou shalt honor thy father and thy mother, that your days may be prolonged in the land..." (Ex. 20:12).

How could this be, you might think? How could a longer life result from honoring the "nest" commandment? A. It is the duty of the saints to cultivate kindness toward all things. The statute brought attention to this principle. See Gal. 5:22-25. "A righteous man has regard for the life of his animal" (Prov. 12:10). B. This practice will always produce a pronounced, uplifting effect on a person's character and leaven his life with greater sweetness. C. After all, the man/woman [family] who shows mercy will receive mercy (Mt. 5:7). D. So it will also be with the influenced society that practices justice with mercy. Where mercy and kindness are universally esteemed and nurtured, Yahweh's approval and blessing will be manifest. E. Elohim blesses obedience, whether or not the ramifications of His ordinances are fully understood. (8) Thus, the commandment to spare the mother provoked thoughtfulness, and as it was obeyed, offered the potential of developing those positive individual and community sympathies that lend themselves to elevated social morality, quality of living, and thereby a longer, healthier life. What may have seemed a small thing was actually a big thing. The great artist Michaelangelo, who was a Believer, once commented: "Trifles make perfection." Better than that, Yeshua said, "Not the smallest letter or stroke shall pass from the Law until all is accomplished" (Mt. 5:18). All the commandments have significance.

Here's another commandment! "...You shall make a parapet for your roof..." (Deut. 22:8).

Here is an example of a practical social mitzvah [single law]. Liabilities and potential hazards, indeed—anything that presented a threat to life and health, waas to be removed or corrected in a Hebrew home to make it comfortable and safe. Parapets were particularly important for preventing visitors who slept on roof tops from rolling off and plummeting to the ground. The idea behind the guidelines concerning houses, vineyards, plowing, and garment materials was to show Israel that YHVH's people must be distinguished in their lives and work by exhibiting quality, thoughtfulness, honesty, wisdom, and thoroughness. And consider this sobering verse: "Not everyone who says to Me 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of My Father who is in heaven" (Mt. 7:21). Selah!

Deuteronomy 22: 9-11 emphasizes the distinction in nature that YHVH made in His creation and that the mixing or blending of distinct things was not sanctioned. There were practical and spiritual reasons for these restrictions. An ox and a donkey were fine for husbandry but ill-suited to plow together. To yoke them, being of differing size, strength, and temperament, would be stressful for them and thus cruel. Sowing different types of seed together tended to produce weaker and fewer crops. Linen and wool were used together in certain pagan superstitious customs, and was thus forbidden. [There are other interesting health reasons. Do some research.] Also, when washed and dried they tended to pull away from one-another. The lesson all this teaches is that YHVH's boundaries must be guarded, and hybridization was to be avoided, especially in the realm of faith. Consider Genesis 6:1-8. Further, the House of Ephraim was exiled and scattered to the nations for hybrid worship--mixing unholy pagan customs with fragments of Torah truth. And, Scripture tells us that Believers should not be yoked with unbelievers. YHVH says, "Can two walk together unless they agree?" (Amos 3:3). His commandments guide and protect. Be glad. The Torah proves the heavenly Father (Abba) loves you.

Conclusion: Elevate Yeshua and place His words above all else. Establish His instructions as central to your life, and ambitions, decisions, and behavior. Love Him. Completely. We've had ample time to pray and repent yet, despite the recent election, spiritual darkness has not yet lifted. It's time to prepare as darkness could still intensify and even restrict free speech and the expression of biblical faith. And grasp this reality, dear reader--heart-felt obedience to His sacred Word is the biblical expression of (a) love, (b) faith, and (c) pure worship. I will see you at the next post. Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church. Shalom.
